primary_claim: Decoding the residual stream at paragraph-transition tokens ('ParaScopes') recovers information about a language model's (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct) upcoming paragraph at a level comparable to being given about 5 tokens of 'cheat' context, well above a random baseline (5.0% broad-subject alignment) but well below full-context regeneration (99.0%), with SONAR ParaScope better preserving broad subject matter and Continuation ParaScope better preserving coherence.

effect.metric: broad subject-match alignment (rubric score 1+) vs baselines
effect.value: SONAR ParaScope 83.2% vs random baseline 5.0% vs full-context regeneration 99.0%; both ParaScope methods roughly comparable to cheat-5 baseline

stated_future_work: Understand why the SONAR ParaScopes often give incoherent outputs, possibly via robustness fine-tuning of SONAR similar to Meta's Large Concept Models paper
Test residual-to-SONAR maps on summed residual streams or intermediate activations (MLP neuron activations, attention pre-out) rather than only residual diffs
Improve training loss for MLP/SONAR ParaScope maps beyond MSE, e.g. using SONAR Decoder CE Loss
Expand the work to longer-horizon planning, e.g. probing n+2 paragraphs or final-state paragraphs
Understand whether the outputs reflect purely correlational 'implicit planning' or also a degree of 'explicit planning'
limitations_stated: Evidence for 'explicit planning' seems weak in Llama 3B; only relatively strong evidence found for 'implicit steering'
SONAR ParaScope often produces incoherent outputs, likely due to its MSE training objective
Continuation ParaScope struggles to retain full context information from a single token's residual stream
Layer-scrubbing and token-locality analyses were based on a small number of examples (e.g. a single A vs B comparison, or 20 texts), so are noisy and preliminary
Metrics used (cosine similarity, BLEURT, rubric scoring) each have known imperfections and don't give a complete picture
quote: Both methods demonstrated performance comparable to having five tokens of "cheat" context, suggesting that language models seem to "plan" or "keep context of" at least that far in advance.
